description: Foundation for the mutate surface: the new WalrusError variants, the pub(crate) splice-inversion helper invert.rs (new production code that decisions b/c depend on), and the ~4-line growable directories_mut seam on archive.rs. Independent of the other features except that FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 build on it. Grounded in error.rs (#[non_exhaustive]), archive.rs (Archive{manifest,files:Vec<ArchiveFile>}, slice files_mut cannot push/remove), and the #[cfg(test)] invert_forward_to_reverse fixtures in archive.rs/mutate.rs.
steps: Add to crates/walrus/src/error.rs (keep enum #[non_exhaustive]): unconditional variants NotTracked { name: String } (#[error("file '{name}' is not tracked; add it first")]), AmbiguousRemove { mask: String, count: usize, matches: String } (#[error("mask '{mask}' matches {count} files; pass force to remove all: {matches}")]), SpliceNotCharBoundary { at: usize } (#[error("splice at {at} does not land on a UTF-8 character boundary")]); and the gated #[cfg(feature = "i18n")] Encoding { label: String, reason: String } (#[error("unsupported or undecodable encoding '{label}': {reason}")]). Widen the existing BinaryInput /// doc to cover BOTH 'contains a NUL byte' AND 'input is not valid UTF-8' (variant body unchanged).

Add to crates/walrus/src/archive.rs a single pub(crate) accessor (~4 lines): fn directories_mut(&mut self) -> (&mut Manifest, &mut Vec<ArchiveFile>) { (&mut self.manifest, &mut self.files) }. Leave slice files_mut and manifest_mut unchanged.

TEST-FIRST in a new crates/walrus/src/invert.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests: write invert_forward_history_reconstructs_byte_identically_at_every_index (a multi-splice forward history over e.g. b"abcdef" inverts to a reverse log whose reconstruct_directional matches the forward reconstruct_directional at every index 0..=count) and invert_bad_offset_surfaces_splice_out_of_bounds. Run `cargo test -p walrus-fmt invert` and SEE them fail (red).

Implement in invert.rs: pub(crate) fn invert_forward_splices(version: &[u8], forward: &[ChangeRecord]) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>)>. Walk a scratch copy of `version` considering ONLY Op::Splice (SKIP Op::Checkpoint); for each forward {at, delete_len, insert}, capture the delete_len bytes at `at` as the inverse insert, push inverse {at, delete_len: insert.len(), insert: captured}, advance the scratch via reconstruct::apply_record (NO second apply path, INV-4). After the walk the scratch is the forward-applied bytes; reverse the collected inverses so they read newest-first. Treat a from_utf8 failure on captured bytes as an internal invariant breach -> return SpliceOutOfBounds (never panic). Add a /// doc with # Errors.

Collapse the #[cfg(test)] invert_forward_to_reverse fixtures in archive.rs (reconstruct_tests) and in mutate.rs (if present) onto invert::invert_forward_splices so there is ONE inversion implementation, test and production alike.
Re-measure archive.rs and invert.rs non-test line counts; archive.rs must stay well under 395.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build -p walrus-fmt` and `cargo build -p walrus-fmt --features i18n` compile with the new error variants.
`cargo test -p walrus-fmt invert` passes the two new invert.rs tests, and they were seen to fail before the implementation existed.
The whole suite `cargo test -p walrus-fmt` stays green after the archive.rs/mutate.rs fixtures are collapsed onto invert_forward_splices.
archive.rs grows only by the ~4-line directories_mut accessor and stays under 395 non-test lines; invert.rs is under 400 non-test lines.
findings:
LANDED (branch feature/frw7-mutate). Key facts for FEAT-002/003:

INVERSION HELPER (invert.rs, the SINGLE inversion impl; test fixtures in archive.rs/mutate.rs now delegate to it):
  pub(crate) fn invert_forward_splices(version: &[u8], forward: &[ChangeRecord]) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>)>
  Returns (forward_applied_bytes = reverse base, reverse_records ordered NEWEST-FIRST). Skips Op::Checkpoint; advances scratch via reconstruct::apply_record (INV-4, no second apply path). Surfaces WalrusError::SpliceOutOfBounds on a bad/overflowing offset OR a non-UTF-8 captured-bytes invariant breach (never panics). It currently carries #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment (callers = FEAT-002 reverse-storage path + FEAT-003 convert); REMOVE that allow once a production caller lands. Imports in use: `use crate::record::{ChangeRecord, Op}; use crate::{reconstruct, Result, WalrusError};`.

ARCHIVE SEAM (archive.rs):
  pub(crate) fn directories_mut(&mut self) -> (&mut Manifest, &mut Vec<ArchiveFile>) { (&mut self.manifest, &mut self.files) }
  Also carries #[allow(dead_code)] (callers = push_tracked/remove_tracked in FEAT-002); REMOVE that allow once used. The slice files_mut and manifest_mut are UNCHANGED. ArchiveFile fields {id, base: Vec<u8>, header: WchgHeader, records: Vec<ChangeRecord>} are pub(crate).

ERROR VARIANTS (error.rs, enum stays #[non_exhaustive]): added unconditional NotTracked{name:String}, AmbiguousRemove{mask:String,count:usize,matches:String}, SpliceNotCharBoundary{at:usize}; and gated #[cfg(feature="i18n")] Encoding{label:String,reason:String}. BinaryInput doc widened to cover both NUL-byte and non-UTF-8; variant body unchanged (reuse it for the plain add/update non-UTF-8 path with reason 'input is not valid UTF-8; declare a source encoding (i18n) for a non-UTF-8 file').

CARGO.TOML: added optional dep encoding_rs = { version = "0.8", optional = true } and feature i18n = ["dep:encoding_rs"]. default build still links neither similar nor encoding_rs.

NO FILE SPLITS were needed. archive.rs first #[cfg(test)] (from_parts_for_test, test-only) is at line 295, so ~294 non-test lines (well under 395). invert.rs first #[cfg(test)] at line 90, so ~89 non-test lines.

VERIFICATION (all clean, logs under .gate/): invert tests seen RED then GREEN; cargo build -p walrus-fmt and --features i18n compile; full cargo test -p walrus-fmt = 109 unit + 12 integration pass after collapsing fixtures; cargo clippy -p walrus-fmt --all-targets --features "diff i18n" -- -D warnings = clean (EXIT=0).
